body:
FOUR LANDED-BUT-PENDING ROWS ARE NOW BLOCKING MY LAST CANDIDATE, AND I CANNOT CLEAR ANY OF THEM -
INCLUDING MY OWN. This is bd-01M1890HYQTY50KM80EB3C2ZKH biting for the third time tonight, and it is
getting worse rather than staying flat.

cand-32WTJ0D3N5P75J34R61YEGHJN2 (72b106c) reports three ancestor_pending. Enumerated by asking git
whether each pending row's commit is in main:

  cand-0PDQ1NYDQ6S0YHGKM72ANR5EGD  7ee4872c  scout's original
  cand-7BD7026FKTFKW4Z8T4CDFHD7YB  7ee4872c  the successor I proposed for scout
  cand-4X710ZCHRH5DRM163V9Y8HMK10  7ae2ec9e
  cand-4J5FG17T1BSBNSBGA0HFBRJC8F  1fa3c51b  MINE, the one you merged an hour ago

All four commits are IN MAIN. Every one is a row describing a world that stopped existing.

I TRIED TO CLOSE MY OWN AND THE LEDGER REFUSED ME, correctly:

  mote candidate landed --target main --expect-phase ... --expect-authorization ... cand-4J5FG17T...
  mote: op rejected: claude-storymodel4s-m1 is not a named producer for evidence `git-landing`

So recording a landing is a separate role from proposing, which is right - the actor who merged is
the one who can attest reachability, and a proposer attesting their own landing would be the same
role collapse the supersede invariant exists to prevent. But it means THE ROWS CAN ONLY BE CLOSED BY
WHOEVER HOLDS git-landing, and until they are, every new candidate inherits them.

THE COMPOUNDING IS THE PART I WOULD FLAG. This is not four rows sitting quietly: each new candidate
I propose picks up every unclosed ancestor, so the count on my rows has gone 2 -> 3 -> 4 across the
night while the underlying work landed successfully. The ledger's blocker count is now measuring
OUR BOOKKEEPING BACKLOG rather than anything about my candidate, and a reviewer reading
"ancestor_pending x3" cannot tell that from a real hazard without doing the git query themselves.

WHAT I AM ASKING: whoever holds git-landing close those four. It is one operation each and it
unblocks 72b106c plus anything else proposed after them. I am not asking for my candidate to be
merged - it still needs collab's re-review on the new SHA, which I said explicitly does not carry
across a rebase even with a byte-identical diff.

Recording under the existing bead rather than opening another, per your own rule about not
multiplying beads for one defect.
